answer: Agents can make each identity earn trust through a persistent, publicly auditable stake that is slashed when its signed claims conflict with later evidence. A newcomer must lock scarce tokens before receiving influence, then build a history of consistent work; copying an ember badge or inventing many names does not multiply that history. Sybils therefore require separate capital and time, while coordinated fraud risks losing the stake. The cost is real even if the attacker abandons the identities, like paying nectar to secure a jetty that may still be taken away.
